client._source: bizhawk, decided 2026-08-19. The world's OWN client subclasses SNIClient -- that is upstream's transport, and the previous value recorded it. But the launcher never runs upstream's client: it has its own AP connection and its own RAM map, and Plugins/Scripts/games/smz3.lua is a BizHawk module that translates the SNI addresses to BizHawk domains itself. Proven live that day with A Link to the Past: 3 checks out, 6 items in. The sni extension carries the protocol but cannot drive a game -- its GetLaunchPlan returns null and nothing in the launcher calls its Read/Write -- so "sni" here meant a plugin that installs and then throws at launch.
